source.author: verg
source.text: Principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis lucentemque globum Lunae Titaniaque astra spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
source.text_original: 'Principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis / lucentemque globum Lunae Titaniaque astra / spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus / mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
source.text_english: First, within the heavens, the lands, the watery plains, the shining orb of the Moon, and the Titanian stars, a spirit nourishes all things from within; poured through its limbs, mind stirs the whole mass and mingles itself with the great body.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: nostrorum primus Maro non longe afuit a ueritate, cuius de summo deo, quem mentem ac spiritum nominauit, haec uerba sunt: principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis lucentemque globum lunae Titaniaque astra spiritus intus alit totamque infusa per artus mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
reuse.text_original: nostrorum primus Maro non longe afuit a ueritate, cuius de summo deo, quem mentem ac spiritum nominauit, haec uerba sunt: principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis lucentemque globum lunae Titaniaque astra spiritus intus alit totamque infusa per artus mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
reuse.text_english: Our Maro was the first not far from the truth, whose words about the highest god, whom he called mind and spirit, are these: in the beginning spirit within nourishes heaven and earth and the watery plains and the shining orb of the moon and Titan’s stars; and mind, poured through the limbs, stirs the whole mass and mingles itself with the great body.
